reason: Perennating plants, roots and buds persist from one growing season to the next; PATO:0104361 perennial life span (EXACT synonym perennial) is the closest term. For buds the sense is narrower (the organ that carries the plant through the unfavourable season).
'without prickles' = no prickles: complement of has_part some prickle (PO:0025169).
Rank = having a strong, offensive smell; FLOPO:0991020 foetid (unpleasant, offensive odour).

target: new: coloured marking (marking pattern spotted PATO_0000333 + colour of the marks red PATO_0000322)
reason: Compound of two values: speckled = spotted (rule C334), and red is the colour of the spots, not of the whole bearer. A term per colour-marking pair would multiply without end.
A satin sheen is a soft lustre of the surface: PATO:0001373 glistening (EXACT synonyms glossy, shiny). Not PATO:0104358 sericeous, which is a covering of silky hairs.
A scoop is a deeply concave blade open at one end, the cochleate shape; PATO:0002208 spoon-shaped (a concave 3-D shape) covers corona segments, lips and corollas.

Semiaquatic plants grow partly in water or in waterlogged ground; this is the FLOPO aquatic value with the approximate qualifier, as for other 'semi-'/'sub-' words. 'semiaquatic or aquatic' is then an ordinary alternative.
PATO:0001354 translucent is already 'exhibiting low opacity', i.e. partly letting light through; 'semi' adds nothing that the term does not cover (as pellucid, rule C237).

target: new: spatial colour gradient (continuum of two colour values along the bearer, cf. continuum in docs/annotation-context-patterns.md)
reason: 'shading to yellow above', 'shading lighter proximally' is a change of colour along the bearer between two values or towards a region, not a quality of its own.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: Comparative of sharp without the teeth or part it is compared with, like 'paler' and 'narrower' (C241, C244).
A comparison of shape with another part ('similar in shape to the pyrene'); usable only when the second part is stated, otherwise rejected as 'similar' (C245).
Slanting = neither erect nor horizontal: PATO:0002481 oblique orientation, whose definition reads 'having a slanting direction or position' (as inclined, C338).
Without stomates: complement of has_part some stomatal complex (PO:0002000, EXACT synonyms stoma, stomate). 'Few or no stomates' is an alternative with frequency.
Strong-scented = having a strong odour, with no hedonic value stated: PATO:0001893 increased odor (child of odorous).

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: 'studded with petiole bases/raphide cells' needs what the bearer is studded with; that part's presence is the annotation, as for 'covered' (C240).
Cernuous = nodding, bending downwards at the top: PATO:0002165 drooping; 'sub-' is the approximate qualifier, as for suborbicular.

There is no cruciform value to approximate (PATO:0001953 decussate is an arrangement), and the three uses (leaf, corolla, nutlets) mean different things. Better to propose 'cruciform' on its own evidence than to make a term from three statements.

target: tertiary leaf vein (PO_0008021); with inflorescence: fourth order inflorescence axis (PO_0025105)
reason: Tertiary picks out a part by its order in a series, not a quality: tertiary veins (French nervures tertiaires) are PO:0008021, and tertiary inflorescence branches are an EXACT synonym of PO:0025105.
'tinged pink' = faintly pink, the same as 'pinkish', which is the colour with the approximate qualifier (like 'greenish').

target: generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to
reason: 'with a tongue' states the presence of a tongue-like projection whose identity depends on the organ (stigma, sheath, corona); there is no general part class, as with 'beak' and 'horn' in the previous review.
Tortuose = tortuous, mapped to PATO:0001989 sinuous (rule C319). In moss descriptions it often means irregularly twisted when dry, which the specimen-condition pattern records.

target: new: coloured marking (marking pattern mottled PATO_0002274 + colour of the marks white PATO_0000323)
reason: Compound of two values: PATO:0002274 mottled, with white as the colour of the patches (Latin albo-maculatus), as for red-speckled.

target: part of the bearer (slot 1 in docs/annotation-context-patterns.md): leaf lamina vein (PO_0020138) + white (PATO_0000323)
reason: White-veined leaves have white veins: the quality white belongs to the veins of the bearer, not to the whole leaf.
Spinules are minute spines and there is no part class for them; 'without spinules' is the negation of PATO:0001365 spiny (spines or similar thin projections on the surface).
Same as 'stomateless': complement of has_part some stomatal complex (PO:0002000, EXACT synonym stomata).

Trigones are thickenings at the corners of bryophyte leaf cell walls; PO and FLOPO have no class for them, so absence cannot be stated without first adding a part class, which three statements do not justify.

label: achlorophyllous
definition: A degree of pigmentation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's lacking chlorophyll, so that it is not green. NOTE: Not PATO:0002249 unpigmented, because achlorophyllous plants and organs often carry other pigments; botany-specific (mycoheterotrophic and parasitic plants).
reason: A clear, well-defined botanical character (holomycotrophic and parasitic plants) with no PATO or FLOPO term; chlorophyll is not a PO part, so a presence/absence rule is not possible.

target: compound of two values (continuum/compound in docs/annotation-context-patterns.md): arched (PATO_0001594) + ascending (PATO_0104355)
reason: Two values run together, as in 'linear-lanceolate': curved like an arch and directed obliquely upward.

target: compound of two values: acute (sensu botany) (FLOPO:0991095) + awn (PO_0025349) present
reason: Acute and ending in an arista: the FLOPO botanical acute plus 'aristate', which is already a rule for awn present (C207).
Stipules or leaves 'joined at the base' are parts of the same kind fused together: FLOPO:0991067 connate (as 'united', C171). The base goes in the part-of-the-bearer slot.
